content:
Reportedly, Apple is piloting a new "Live Notes" system at some of its retail stores. According to the latest reports, the system uses artificial intelligence technology to record and transcribe service conversations between the Genius Bar staff and customers.

Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman pointed out in the latest issue of his "Power On" newsletter that the Live Notes system allows Apple store employees to "use AI tools to record service conversations, and transcribe and summarise the exchanges with customers into summaries".

The transcripts are subsequently stored in Apple's internal Genius Bar system. Bloomberg reported that the move is aimed at allowing employees to focus on customer service itself without being distracted by taking notes of the conversations.

Reportedly, Live Notes must obtain consent from both employees and customers before audio recording can be activated during Genius Bar service conversations.

However, Apple retail staff are reportedly worried about how the Live Notes system might be used in the future:

As of now, Live Notes is not mandatory. Bloomberg indicated that it remains "unclear" whether Apple will roll out the system to more stores, make it mandatory, or change the way the transcripts are used.
